entities.summary: János Vitéz de Zredna was a Hungarian and Croat humanist, diplomat, Latinist, mathematician, astrologist and astronomer. He served as Archbishop of Esztergom from 1465 until his death. János Vitéz de Zredna was born in 1408 in Križevci, a town in the Kingdom of Croatia, which is now part of modern-day Croatia. He studied in the city of Sibenik, and later in the city of Padua, Italy, where he earned his degree in law and philosophy. After returning to Croatia, he became a prominent figure in the country's government and education systems. He was appointed as the Archbishop of Esztergom in 1465, a position he held until his death in 1472. As Archbishop, Vitéz de Zredna played a crucial role in promoting education and cultural exchange between Hungary and Croatia. He also worked to improve the country's economic and military situation. Vitéz de Zredna was a prolific writer and left behind a significant legacy in the fields of law, philosophy, and science. He was also known for his diplomatic skills and played a key role in maintaining peace and stability in the region during a time of great turmoil. Despite his many accomplishments, Vitéz de Zredna's life was marked by controversy and power struggles, which ultimately led to his downfall. He died on August 15, 1472, at the age of 64. Vitéz de Zredna's legacy continues to be felt in modern-day Hungary and Croatia, where he is remembered as a great leader and scholar. His contributions to the fields of law, philosophy, and science have had a lasting impact on the region, and his name remains synonymous with intellectual and cultural achievement.
